notes:
SERIES CONTRACT — this template compares exactly three instruments: CHPY, SMH, SOX.
It renders nothing else: columns outside the SERIES whitelist in the script are ignored and a
missing one is reported on screen.

ASSISTANT: BEFORE emitting this applet you MUST create its data files — they are never saved
with the template and may have been deleted since the last run. Do not look for or reuse any
other file (semi_compare*, etf_prices*, *_hist* …). Do not emit the applet until both exist:

  chpy_smh_sox.csv        header exactly: date,chpy,smh,sox   (lowercase; one row per trading
                          day, oldest first; ISO dates; daily closes; only days all three have)
  chpy_smh_sox_meta.json  {"title":"CHPY vs SMH vs SOX","note":"<source + date range>",
                          "series":{"chpy":{"label":"CHPY","desc":"YieldMax Semiconductor
                          Portfolio Option Income ETF","color":"#ef4444"},"smh":{"label":"SMH",
                          "desc":"VanEck Semiconductor ETF","color":"#4a9eff"},"sox":{"label":
                          "SOX","desc":"PHLX Semiconductor Index","color":"#f59e0b"}}}
                          — exactly these three series entries, no others.

Source: Yahoo Finance via run_python (urllib, User-Agent header), one call per symbol:
  https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/<SYM>?range=1y&interval=1d
  with SYM = CHPY, SMH, %5ESOX (^SOX); closes are result[0].indicators.quote[0].close,
  dates from result[0].timestamp (UTC). Write both files to the project root (cwd).
Fetch exactly these three symbols. Never add SOXX, NVDA, AMD, TSM, ASML, MU or any other
ticker, index or ETF. Never rename or reorder columns. Never change the file names.
Then output this template VERBATIM.
